question:
**Case Study 2: Supply Chain Optimization for a Factory**

A factory produces three products P1, P2, and P3 using three resources R1, R2, and R3. The consumption ($\times$100 units) is given by the following table (each entry denotes units of resource used per product):

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline & P1 & P2 & P3 \\ \hline R1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline R2 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ \hline R3 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline\end{array}$

Each day, the availability of resources is R1: 400 units, R2: 600 units, R3: 300 units.

a) Write the system of equations in matrix form.

b) Determine, using the matrix method, how many batches ($x$, $y$, $z$) of P1, P2, P3 (in 100s) can be produced daily, so all resources are exactly used up.

c) If due to supply chain disruption, R2's availability is reduced to 300 units, determine whether a solution exists and, if so, find it or otherwise comment on the consistency of the system.
explanation:
a)

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be number of batches (in 100s) for P1, P2, P3.

So, the equations:
$2x + y + z = 4$
$y + 2z = 6$
$x + z = 3$

Matrix form: $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 6 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$

b)

Find $|A|$:
$|A| = 2 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} - 1 \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} + 1 \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix}$
$= 2(1\times1-2\times0) - (0\times1 - 2\times1) + (0\times0 - 1\times1)$
$= 2(1) - (0-2) + (0-1)$
$= 2 + 2 - 1 = 3$

Non-zero: unique solution

Calculate $A^{-1}$ using minors and cofactors (detailed steps):

$A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

Cofactor matrix:

$C_{11} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 1(1)-2(0)=1$
$C_{12} = -\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -[0(1)-2(1)] = -(-2)=2$
$C_{13} = \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = 0(0)-1(1)=-1$
$C_{21} = -\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -[1(1)-1(0)]=-[1] = -1$
$C_{22} = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 2(1)-1(1)=2-1=1$
$C_{23} = -\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = -[2(0)-1(1)] = -(-1)=1$
$C_{31} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 1(2)-1(1)=2-1=1$
$C_{32} = -\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = -[2(2)-1(0)] = -[4]= -4$
$C_{33} = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 2(1)-1(0)=2$

Cofactor Matrix $C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

Adjugate: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$

$A^{-1} = \frac{1}{3} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$

$X = A^{-1}B = \frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 6 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}$

Row 1: $1\times4 + (-1)\times6 + 1\times3 = 4-6+3=1$
Row 2: $2\times4 + 1\times6 + (-4)\times3=8+6-12=2$
Row 3: $-1\times4 + 1\times6 + 2\times3 = -4+6+6=8$

So, $X=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 8\end{bmatrix}= \begin{bmatrix}1/3 \\ 2/3 \\ 8/3 \end{bmatrix}$

So batches: P1: $33.33$ units, P2: $66.67$ units, P3: $266.67$ units.

c)

Availability changes to $[4,3,3]^T$:
$B' = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$

$X = A^{-1} B' = \frac{1}{3} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$

Row 1: $1\times4 + (-1)\times3 + 1\times3= 4-3+3=4$
Row 2: $2\times4 + 1\times3 + (-4)\times3 = 8+3-12=-1$
Row 3: $-1\times4 + 1\times3 + 2\times3 = -4+3+6=5$

So $X=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}4/3 \\ -1/3 \\ 5/3\end{bmatrix}$

Negative value for $y$ (batches of P2), so though mathematically a solution exists, **it is not physically feasible** (can't produce negative batches). The system is consistent, but infeasible in the context of production!

options.A:
a) $\begin{bmatrix}2&1&1\\0&1&2\\1&0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\6\\3\end{bmatrix}$
b) $x=\frac13$, $y=\frac23$, $z=\frac83$.
c) For reduced R2, $x=\frac43$, $y=\frac13$, $z=\frac53$, so the system is feasible.
options.B:
a) $\begin{bmatrix}2&1&1\\0&1&2\\1&0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\6\\3\end{bmatrix}$
b) $x=\frac13$, $y=\frac23$, $z=\frac83$.
c) For reduced R2, $x=\frac43$, $y=-\frac13$, $z=\frac53$; the system is mathematically consistent but physically infeasible because $y$ is negative.
options.C:
a) $\begin{bmatrix}2&0&1\\1&1&0\\1&2&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\6\\3\end{bmatrix}$
b) $x=\frac83$, $y=\frac23$, $z=\frac13$.
c) For reduced R2, no mathematical solution exists because $|A|=0$.
options.D:
a) $\begin{bmatrix}2&1&1\\0&1&2\\1&0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\6\\3\end{bmatrix}$
b) Since $|A|=0$, the original system has infinitely many solutions.
c) The reduced-resource system is inconsistent and has no solution.
